title: User | thepilotnews.com - "I Bet You Think You Can't Get Scammed Online: 7 Ways to Get Your Life Back After Losing Your Money in Crypto" By Josée Marleau
text:
Award-Winning Author Josée Marleau Raises Awareness About the Rising Threat of Online Scams Scams targeting consumers continue to grow in both frequency and financial impact. In the United States, the Federal Trade Commission reported that consumers lost more than $12.5 billion to fraud in 2024, while newer data shows losses tied to scams originating on social media reached $2.1 billion in 2025 alone. In Canada, the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre reported more than $704 million in fraud losses in 2025, with investment fraud accounting for the largest share. From imposter schemes and online shopping fraud to increasingly sophisticated crypto and relationship scams, today’s fraud landscape is evolving rapidly—often leaving victims emotionally shaken as well as financially harmed.
“One thing I learned from my experience is that these swindles do not begin with outrageous demands for large sums of money,” said Josée Marleau, award-winning author of I Bet You Think You Can't Get Scammed Online: 7 Ways to Get Your Life Back After Losing Your Money in Crypto . “They begin with stories designed to pull at your emotions, earn your trust, and lower your defenses. It is not about getting you to send money immediately. It is about building a relationship that makes the lie feel believable.”
Having endured fraud firsthand, Josée brings uncommon credibility and urgency to the conversation around online scams and financial deception. Through her writing, she pairs personal experience with practical guidance, helping readers understand how modern fraud schemes work and why they can be so persuasive. Her book, I Bet You Think You Can't Get Scammed Online , examines the emotional and psychological tactics scammers use to build trust, manipulate judgment, and exploit vulnerability. Drawing from her own recovery journey, Josée offers readers warning signs to watch for, questions to ask before investing, and strategies to help determine whether an opportunity is legitimate—or a costly trap.
“I have experienced financial loss and fallen victim to this kind of fraud, and it deeply affected my personal life,” said Josée. “As I looked more closely at these schemes, it became clear that there is a psychology behind them. When people understand that psychology, they are better equipped to protect themselves and reduce their risk. As part of my mission to raise awareness, I have built a community focused on supporting victims and helping people recognize and avoid these fraudsters before more damage is done.”
In addition to her work as an author, Josée is building an online community through social media and educational programming designed to help people better understand, identify, and recover from fraud. She also hosts workshops that explore the warning signs of scams, the psychology behind manipulation, and the steps individuals can take to protect themselves and rebuild with confidence. To book Josée for a speaking engagement or to learn more about upcoming workshops, please contact: joseemarleaucoach@gmail.com
Josée Marleau’s book is available on Amazon .
